memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "The frogs will leave you and your houses, your officials and your people; they will remain only in the Nile." After Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh, Moses cried out to the Lord about the frogs he had brought on Pharaoh. And the Lord did what Moses asked." - Exodus 8:11-13a (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses cried out to the Lord, and the Lord did what Moses asked. That short sentence carries enormous weight.

Notice first that Moses prayed for his oppressor. He had every human reason to want Pharaoh to suffer longer. Instead he took the request seriously and cried out to God on his behalf.

Notice second that God answered precisely. Not roughly, not partially — the frogs left the houses exactly as promised, remaining only in the Nile where they belonged. Our God is not careless with detail.

And notice the manner of Moses' praying: he cried out. This was not a formality. Even when praying for an enemy, he prayed with his whole heart.

James tells us the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective, and points to Elijah, a man just like us (Jas 5:16-17). Moses was not a special category of human being. He was a man who took God at His word and prayed.

Whom do you find it hardest to pray for? That may be exactly where to begin today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I willing to pray sincerely for someone who has wronged me?
2. Do my prayers reflect real crying out, or only routine?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to pray honestly and wholeheartedly, even for those I find hard to love. Amen.
